Special education advocacy

For special education advocates

The winning argument is almost always the same: the district's own evaluation found something the IEP does not address. Finding it means reading a 40-page evaluation against a 20-page IEP, line by line. That is the part Countercite does.

Join the early list

What it does on an IEP case

Evaluation against IEP

Every finding, recommendation and area of need in the district's evaluation, matched to the goal, service or accommodation that addresses it — and a list of the ones that nothing addresses.

Goals that cannot be measured

A goal without a baseline, a criterion or a measurement method is a goal that cannot be enforced later. These get flagged as written.

Service minutes, added up

What the IEP promises versus what the service grid actually totals. They disagree more often than anyone expects.

The IDEA clock

Evaluation timelines, meeting notice periods, consent windows and response deadlines, tracked per case and per state.

The families you currently turn away

The research on advocate pricing says plainly that cost is a substantial barrier and that the system is stacked against low and middle-income families. That is unmet demand at your current price — not a marketing problem, a capacity problem.

Halving the hours a case takes does two things at once: it raises your effective hourly rate on full-fee work, and it makes sliding-scale work possible on cases you would otherwise have to decline.

Questions advocates ask

Does it decide eligibility or placement?
No, and it is built not to. Eligibility and placement are team decisions under IDEA. Countercite surfaces what the documents say and where they conflict; the argument and the judgement are yours.
Is student data safe?
Documents are encrypted, never used for training, and deletable per case. You should still confirm your own obligations to the families you serve — advocates are not always covered by the same rules as districts.
Does it work for 504 plans too?
Yes. The same comparison applies: what the evaluation found against what the plan provides.

Test it on a case you won

Upload an evaluation and IEP from a case you already argued. See whether the contradiction list matches your notes.
